title: Formalism and New Criticism: reading the poem on its own terms

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: Which school does each idea belong to?

explain.say: Imagine walking past the same tree every day until you stop seeing it. In 1917 the Russian critic Viktor Shklovsky said art exists to make you see the tree again. Formalists and New Critics study how a text works, its devices and shape, not the author's life. See the three groups on the board?

explain.say: First group: Russian Formalism. Defamiliarisation means making the familiar strange, so you notice it. Tolstoy once told a story through the eyes of a horse. Fabula is the story in time order, syuzhet is the order the text tells it. Can you think of a film that begins at the end?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which school does each idea belong to?

explain.say: Second group: the New Critics in Britain and America. Cleanth Brooks read Donne's poem The Canonization, which opens: For God's sake hold your tongue, and let me love. He found paradox and irony knitted into one whole, like a well-made urn. That is organic unity. What paradox can you spot in lovers called saints?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which school does each idea belong to?

explain.say: Third group: the mistakes they warned against. The intentional fallacy is judging a poem by what the author meant. The affective fallacy is confusing it with your feelings. The heresy of paraphrase says a poem cannot be boiled down to a prose summary. Which one tempts you most?

explain.say: Here are the milestones on a timeline. From the 1970s critics turned away, saying New Criticism ignored history, gender and race. But every time you analyse one word in an exam, you use its tools. Brilliant. Challenge: describe your own kitchen as if you had never seen one before.

faq.a: Shklovsky's idea from 1917 that art makes familiar things strange again, so that we perceive them freshly instead of on autopilot.
Wimsatt and Beardsley argued in 1946 that the author's intention is neither available nor a reliable standard for judging a poem. The words on the page are the evidence.

faq.q: What did New Critics mean by organic unity?
faq.a: That every part of a good poem, its images, sounds, ironies and tensions, works together into one whole, as the parts of a living thing do.

faq.q: What is the heresy of paraphrase?
faq.a: Cleanth Brooks's phrase for the mistake of thinking a poem's meaning can be stated in a prose summary. The meaning lives in the poem's exact form.
asks: Why can you not summarise a poem?

faq.q: Why did critics turn against New Criticism?
faq.a: From the 1970s, critics argued it treated poems as sealed objects, ignoring history, politics, gender, race and readers. Its close reading methods survived anyway.
asks: What are the weaknesses of New Criticism?

facts: Shklovsky's essay Art as Device was published in 1917.
Wimsatt and Beardsley published The Intentional Fallacy in 1946.
Cleanth Brooks took the title The Well Wrought Urn (1947) from Donne's poem The Canonization.
